profile.headline: Accessibility Software Engineer
profile.summary: I am a first-generation Mexican American who studied Computer Science, Political Science, and Ethnic Studies at Cal Poly San Luis Obispo. I lead with passion and vulnerability to foster community and create comfortable spaces for collaboration. I believe in coding ethically and ensuring that the products of our knowledge are creating a positive impact for all communities.

positions.title: BEACoN Research Scholar
positions.description:
Project: Breaking the Binary is a multi-strand research project aimed to address the disparities within the CPE program to create a more radically inclusive CPE program and culture. 
• Collaborated in a cross-disciplinary team to integrate a trauma-informed, anti-racist interviewing protocol to survey and engage with students in the CPE program
• Influenced the faculty focused strand to include culturally responsive teaching survey at the collegiate level
• Our team will be attending the Society for Social Studies of Science (4S) conference virtually in October to present our completed protocol and methodology

company.name: California Polytechnic State University-San Luis Obispo

positions.title: Student Research Assistant
positions.description:
• Programming website using HTML and CSS to present the Mechanical Engineering Department’s research project to bridge the understanding gap between underrepresented students and introductory STEM classes
• Assisting development of the Adaptive Learning Modules through Concept Warehouse using PHP that will be used for California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo’s College of Engineering introduction STEM courses.

positions.title: Sponsorship Co-Director
positions.description:
• Co-founded and organized Cal Poly’s first UX conference with a creative competition for participants to learn more about UX in an inclusive environment. Over the course of 2 weekends, students will attend workshops, presentations, and create a project in teams.
• Lead a sponsorship team of 5 members to develop sponsorship acquisition strategy and foster professional mentorship relationships, interacting with 20+ professionals.
• Maintain event reports, team expenses, and raised collectively $4000+ in company sponsorships and donations

positions.title: Data Science Fellow
positions.description:
• DS4A is a competitive, merit-based 13-week program designed and taught by instructors from Harvard and MIT
• Aims to create a nationwide ecosystem of talented, traditionally under-represented minorities in full-stack data science principles and applied contexts through a case-based curriculum and hands-on training.

positions.title: Facility Supervisor
positions.description:
• Provide daily operations for the Recreation Center as assigned. Know the unique policies and procedures that govern the facility
• Educate participants and staff on all policies and procedures. Have the ability to explain policy, and the theory that supports policies
• Open, close, and secure facilities at prescribed times and inspect the facility for safety and maintenance concerns

volunteerExperiences.description:
As a first-generation woman of color, I struggled to envision myself in the tech industry, and I limited myself from pursuing computer science straight of high school due to my imposter syndrome and not seeing anyone look like me in tech. It was due to my Professor's encouragement and investment in my education that inspired me to pursue my interest in computer science and I want to give back to the community and be there for high school students that perhaps had similar struggles as myself.

• Remotely taught Java Fundamentals to a class of 30 students that are majority first-generation, Latinx, and womxn.
• Completed 30 hours of training to learn teaching pedagogy and course work for AP Computer Science A.
• Encouraged and advised students as well about the college process by meeting with them 1:1 after school hours.

As Commissioner of Philanthropy, I continued my love for community service by organizing and hosting service events along with my peers. During my time, I organized and/or contributed:

• Thanksgiving Food Drive
We collected and donated 24 Thanksgiving Meal Bags to CAPSLO to support Head Start Families during the holiday season.
• Kirk Elementary School Drive
Our chapter alone raised over 900 school supplies for Kirk Elementary in Fresno, California when we went to over to one of our national conferences. That was our most successful school drive thanks to our consistent social media campaign to get donations.
• Teddy Land
I was in charge of our table set up for the annual college fair that we host for underrepresented students to educate and support them in their pursuit for higher education.
